newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures took their direction from the Bund market on Monday and drifted gently lower throughout the session amid subdued volume and caution ahead of week packed with U.S. data releases.

The December future settled down 0.20 at 126.28 close to the low of the day at 126.24, although volume was a meagre 54,064 contracts, the lowest since September 30. Traders said technical levels had been been a primary focus during the session.
Traders said the five-year area of the curve attracted good two-way interest, the net result being outperformance over Germany with the spread moving as high as minus nine.
One trader at a French bank said non-residents had sold French five-year bonds for German bonds, as was the case on Friday, on the view such a negative spread was unsustainable.

Another trader said, however, there had been good interest in the French five-year area from other investors. The spread was at minus seven basis points at 1600 GMT compared with minus four on Friday.

He lamented the lack of interest in the futures market and said he feared it would remain lacklustre for the rest of the week. "Friday will be the only interesting day and we're closed for a holiday," he said.
The U.S. statistics bonanza starts on Tuesday with third quarter employment cost figures, October consumer confidence and the Johnson Redbook survey of retail sales.

On Wednesday, the first estimate of third quarter U.S. GDP, exected to show a slowdown, will be released. Economists polled by Reuters predicited a 1.8 percent quarter-on-quarter increase compared with 4.7 percent in the previous period.

Analysts said the most significant report would be the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for October due on Friday. The French Matif exchange will be closed for a public holiday although there will be some futures trading on GLOBEX during the day.
The 10-year spread between French and German remained unchanged at minus four basis points.

Iain Lindsay, bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais, said the TEC 10 floating rate 2006 OAT looked expensive relative to its theoretical value following a period of interest from domestic investors with spare cash to invest.

December continued to trade within a narrow range, unable to break through the contract high of 96.47, while hopes for a Bank of France intervention rate cut as soon as this week prevented any significant declines, traders said.

With hopes of a near-term German interest rate cut fading, following the numerous bearish statements from Bundesbank officials, December PIBOR managed to outperform its German counterpart. The spread narrowed to 36 basis points.
The yield on 13-week Treasury bills fell to 3.25 percent from 3.27 percent last week at Monday's regular auction.
The franc also traded in a fairly narrow range. It was at 3.3785 per mark late on Monday compared with 3.3775 late on Friday.
Call money was unchanged at 3-1/4 3/8 percent.
